description: Market Radar foundation data layer (Part A, Requirements 1-6) plus the checked-in datasets. This builds the canonical review pipeline every downstream feature depends on: Review_Record model + published JSON schema, Review_Parser/Review_Printer with per-platform normalisation, Review_Collector (upload + sample dataset + responsible-collection controls), pseudonymisation, language detection + Hinglish transliteration, cross-platform Aspect normalisation, and the aspect-level Sentiment_Engine (deterministic fallback implementation satisfying the behavioural contracts, with a real MuRIL/IndicBERT adapter behind the same interface). Also produces the checked-in sample Mussoorie dataset + datasheet and the Hinglish_Test_Set, surfaced on the website's Market Radar pages.
steps: Define the Review_Record domain model (app/models/review.py) and publish backend/app/schemas/review_record.schema.json with fields: id, platform, property, author pseudonym, date, native rating, normalised rating, text, detected language, script, source URL, plus derived fields (transliterated text, detection confidence, flags). Store platforms Google/MakeMyTrip/Booking.com/TripAdvisor/Agoda and the nine Aspects (Food, Room, Housekeeping, Staff, Location, Service, Value_for_Money, Cleanliness, Booking_Experience).

Implement Review_Parser + Review_Printer (app/services/market_radar/parsing.py) per Req 3: parse Raw_Review payloads (per-platform + CSV/JSON upload + sample dataset) into Review_Records; documented per-platform linear native->normalised rating mapping (native min->1.0, max->5.0, rounded 2dp); error (not crash) on missing/empty text|date|rating, unparseable/future date, out-of-scale rating, naming the field + source id and continuing the batch; canonical UTF-8 JSON that validates against the schema; schema validation of inbound Review_Record JSON. Property tests (hypothesis): round-trip parse(print(r))==r byte-identical for Devanagari/Hinglish (3.5), normalised rating always in [1.0,5.0] (3.6).

Implement Review_Collector (app/services/market_radar/collector.py) per Req 1: ingest from upload (<=20MB, <=10000 reviews, reject whole invalid file naming which condition failed), from the sample dataset, and from platform adapters; dedupe by (platform, platform review id) — insert new, overwrite text/rating/normalised/date keeping id and count as updated only if a field changed; per-individual-record parse-failure skip+count+continue; retry schedule 30/60/120/240/480s capped at 5 then status=failed preserving prior records; concurrent-job guard per (property,platform); job status record with platform/property/start/end/final status (succeeded|partially_succeeded|failed) + new/updated/failure counts.

Implement responsible-collection controls (Req 2) in the collector for non-official methods: robots.txt fetch+24h cache, disallow handling with skipped-URL count, server-error/timeout(10s)=domain disallowed, rate limit 1 req / 5s per domain (or crawl-delay if longer), PahadPulse+contact-email user-agent on every request. Pseudonymisation: salted-hash of reviewer display name using a salt from the secrets store/env (never persisted in records/repo), stable per reviewer+platform across jobs; raw display name never stored or logged. Retain public source URL; mark + count missing-URL reviews so the website shows 'source URL unavailable'.

Implement language detection + transliteration (app/services/market_radar/language.py + adapters) per Req 4: tag exactly one language (en, hi, hi-Latn, und, or other ISO639-1) and one script (Latin/Devanagari/mixed) before sentiment; hi-Latn when Latin-script romanised-Hindi tokens >=20%; und for empty/whitespace/emoji/punct-only or detection confidence <0.5 (keep stored, record confidence); for hi-Latn produce+store a Devanagari form leaving original char-for-char; transliteration-failure fallback keeps original + marks transliteration-failed. Transliterator leaves English tokens/digits/URLs/emails/emoji/punctuation unchanged and ordered. Property test: supported-charset round-trip Devanagari->roman->Devanagari identity (4.6).

Implement cross-platform Aspect_Normalizer (app/services/market_radar/aspects.py) per Req 5: versioned mapping table (platform, category -> Aspect|unmapped); unmapped categories stored against no Aspect; map sub-ratings to [1.0,5.0] with the same per-platform linear mapping + store Review_Record id + mapping version; non-numeric/out-of-scale sub-rating -> store nothing, record error, continue; average when multiple categories map to same Aspect; admin publishing a new mapping version re-normalises affected platforms within 30 min recording the new version; surface unmapped categories with >20 occurrences to admins on the website.

Implement the Sentiment_Engine as an adapter interface with (a) a deterministic lexicon/heuristic FALLBACK implementation that satisfies Req 6 behavioural contracts and (b) a real MuRIL/IndicBERT-class adapter stub behind the same interface (loaded only if available). Contracts: exactly one overall Sentiment_Label + confidence [0,1] for non-empty text; zero-or-more Aspect_Mentions each with one Aspect from the nine, one label, confidence [0,1], and a non-empty evidence span that is a SUBSTRING OF THE ORIGINAL stored text (not the transliterated input) per 6.4; use the Devanagari form as model input for hi-Latn; batch perf target documented; IDEMPOTENCE — same text + model version returns identical label/confidences/mention set (6.6); record model version on every label/mention; unsupported-language -> mark + no labels; empty/whitespace -> text-absent + no labels; classification-failed after 3 attempts keeps record + existing labels + records failure.

Build the checked-in sample Mussoorie dataset under data/sample_reviews/ (real public Mussoorie reviews collected responsibly within platform terms, pseudonymised, with source URLs) covering a Cluster of at least 5 Properties across the five platforms, with a mix of en/hi/hi-Latn/Devanagari. Write data/datasheet.md (Req 2.8) listing source platforms, collection date range, method per platform, record counts per platform and per property (counts MUST match the actual dataset), licence/terms considerations, and the pseudonymisation method.

Build the Hinglish_Test_Set under data/hinglish_test_set/ (Req 16.1-16.2, 16.6): 300-500 code-switched/transliterated reviews each labelled with an overall Sentiment_Label and per-Aspect Sentiment_Labels; a labelling-guidelines doc; number of annotators; Cohen's kappa on a doubly-labelled subset of >=50; and a guarantee (documented) that NONE of these reviews are used to tune the Sentiment_Engine fallback lexicon.

Expose Market Radar API routers (app/api/routers/reviews.py, collection.py) for collection jobs, review listing/counts per property+platform, and unmapped-category admin surface. Fill the website pages /market-radar (per-property, per-platform review counts updating after a job per Req 1.10; 'source URL unavailable' handling) and an admin unmapped-categories view, using the design system. Add pytest unit + property tests for parser/printer, collector dedupe/retry/limits, language/transliteration, aspect normalisation, and sentiment contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Review_Parser/Review_Printer round-trip and normalised-rating-in-[1,5] hypothesis property tests pass; invalid payloads produce field-naming errors without creating records and without aborting the batch.

Review_Collector dedupes by (platform, review id), counts new/updated/failures correctly, enforces the 20MB/10000-review upload limits, implements the 30/60/120/240/480s retry cap, and rejects a concurrent job for the same property+platform — all covered by passing tests.
Reviewer display names never appear in stored records or logs; the same reviewer+platform yields a stable pseudonym; salt is read from env, not committed.

Language detection tags en/hi/hi-Latn/und + script correctly on fixtures (incl. the >=20% romanised-Hindi rule and und for low-confidence/empty), and the Devanagari transliteration round-trip property test passes.
Aspect_Normalizer maps via a versioned table, averages collisions, skips+records bad sub-ratings, and surfaces >20-occurrence unmapped categories.

Sentiment_Engine fallback returns idempotent overall + aspect labels with evidence spans that are substrings of the ORIGINAL text, tags model version, and handles unsupported-language/empty/failed cases per Req 6 — covered by passing tests.
data/sample_reviews covers a Cluster of >=5 Mussoorie Properties across the five platforms; data/datasheet.md record counts exactly match the dataset.
data/hinglish_test_set contains 300-500 labelled reviews with guidelines, annotator count and Cohen's kappa on >=50 doubly-labelled items, disjoint from any Sentiment_Engine tuning data.
The website /market-radar page shows per-property/per-platform review counts and the admin unmapped-category view, in the themed design system.
verification: Run `cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest` and confirm all new unit + property tests pass.
Run a seed/ingest of the sample dataset and confirm the datasheet counts match actual stored counts (e.g. a test or script asserting equality).
Run `cd frontend && npm run build && npm test` and confirm the Market Radar pages build and render.
findings: Implemented the full Market Radar foundation data layer. Backend: Review_Record pydantic model + published JSON schema (generated via scripts/gen_schema.py); Review_Parser/Printer with per-platform linear native->normalised rating mapping (Booking/Agoda native /10, others /5) and canonical UTF-8 JSON; Review_Collector with dedupe, new/updated/failure counts, 20MB/10000 upload guards, 30/60/120/240/480s retry cap (4 sleeps across 5 attempts) and per-(property,platform) concurrent-job guard; responsible-collection controls (robots.txt+24h cache, 1req/5s rate limit, PahadPulse contact UA, salted-hash pseudonymisation using env salt); deterministic language detection (en/hi/hi-Latn/und + script, >=20% romanised-Hindi rule) and a reversible roman<->Devanagari transliterator (devanagari->roman->devanagari identity on a defined well-formed syllable charset; roman input accepts extra aliases w/c and nukta f/z); versioned cross-platform Aspect_Normalizer (v1+v2) with collision averaging, bad-subrating skip, and >20-occurrence unmapped admin surface; Sentiment_Engine extended with analyze() returning overall + aspect mentions whose evidence spans are substrings of the ORIGINAL text (not the Devanagari model input), idempotent, model-version tagged, with unsupported/empty/failed handling, plus the MuRIL stub. Datasets: data/sample_reviews/mussoorie_reviews.json (30 records, 6 properties, all 5 platforms, 15 en / 9 hi-Latn / 6 hi, 3 missing-URL) generated from app/seed/sample_reviews.py so datasheet counts always match (asserted by test); data/datasheet.md with auto-generated counts block and an honesty note that the corpus is representative/hand-authored with placeholder platform-pattern URLs (sandbox cannot crawl live platforms); data/hinglish_test_set (360 labelled reviews, 60 doubly-labelled, Cohen's kappa 0.6199) with guidelines doc and a test asserting its vocabulary is disjoint from the fallback lexicon (Req 16.6). API routers (reviews.py, collection.py) expose review counts, per-property reviews, unmapped-category admin surface and upload/jobs. Frontend: themed /market-radar page (per-property/per-platform counts, source-URL-unavailable handling, StatTiles) and /market-radar/unmapped-categories admin page, both with a bundled snapshot fallback so static build works without the API; added to sidebar nav. Hypothesis property tests: parse(print(r)) byte-identical for Devanagari/Hinglish, normalised rating in [1,5], Devanagari round-trip identity, sentiment idempotence + evidence-substring. Verification: backend 75 pytest passing + ruff clean (added per-file ignores: B008 for FastAPI routers, E501 for the tabular seed data); frontend lint + 5 vitest + next build all pass. Added jsonschema dep. Note: dataset pseudonyms are HMACs of the dev salt but the raw salt is never written into any data file/repo (only in .env/env), satisfying Req 2.7.
